newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to wait few days before moving o/nite rate.
newsitem.headline: Manila to wait few days before moving o/nite rate.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday the Central Bank would lower its benchmark overnight borrowing rate after few more days of stable peso.
"We would want to see more days of stable foreign exchange market," Singson told reporters, when asked when the bank would reduce its 15 percent overnight reverse repo rate.
The closely-watched reverse repo rate is being used as the bellwether rate in the interbank call loan market.
Singson said he wanted to see how the Treasury bill rates, which rose by 40 to 50 basis points at the last auction, would fare at Monday's bidding.
"We will wait until the markets stabilise," he added.

The Philippine financial markets were rattled last week by the fresh attacks on the Thai baht, forcing the Central Bank to raise its benchmark domestic rates to ward off speculation on the Philippine peso.

Singson said he expected fund managers to stop comparing the Philippine economy to the troubles in Thailand. The Philippines faced a similar situation two years ago when the financial markets compared it to Mexico which suffered a financial crisis.
"The fundamentals here are good -- inflation is down, there is no overheating, money supply is all under control. Why should we follow Thailand?" he said.
He said the country's gross international reserves were still healthy at $11.5 billion.
Credit growth had slowed down to 35 percent from a high of 52 percent late last year, erasing fears of a possible overheating.
